catalogue_requests.reason: cap.motion.home.v1 binds robot.arm or motion.axis, not robot.gripper, so no catalogue class can home this hand; the extension has no input and returns homed and width_mm.

cap.motion.joint_position.v1 and cap.motion.stop.v1 bind robot.arm or motion.axis, not robot.gripper; a two-finger width move has no catalogue class, so the extension carries a bounded width_mm input (0..80).
cap.motion.stop.v1 binds robot.arm, robot.mobile_base or motion.axis, not robot.gripper; the safe-state stop that drives the fingers fully open is therefore an extension with no input.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by a model-authored, unreviewed package; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level, and nothing ran on hardware or on the upstream physics engine. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names the PythonObjectDriver helper, but this package is a direct Driver (the card's decision is direct-driver) because the inputs need the mm-to-m native-unit conversion and the state is the upstream GripperStateData dataclass; no family grammar is used. The card preferred the upstream simulator, but the task forbids importing or running code from the read-only clone, so the package fake is the only backend. Scope: only the simulated Franka Hand (franka_sim.gripper.physics:FrankaHandPhysics) is bound. The arm FCI bridge, the FrankaGripperServer wire protocol, MobileDuoRunner and SpineStubServer are not covered, so their arrays and network transports are NOT COVERED. The fake has no physics, no scene and no blocking settle; width changes instantly and force/speed are accepted only for signature compatibility, which is why the driver exposes width and not force. The 5 mm grasp epsilon band is the upstream physics-test convention (tests/test_gripper_physics.py:124), not a device limit. The hand's 0.08 m stroke is published by the catalogue class in mm, so the three Limits declare 80 mm and cite docs/robot-state.md:202; G4 therefore reports three REF_VALUE warnings (it compares the literal 80 with the literal 0.08 on the cited line). The cited line states 0.08 m and 8 cm, the same bound converted to the class's mm unit; no value was invented. The other warnings are none. The fake's object_width and all start values are test data marked placeholder. The package has no hardware backend and declares R2 because the gripper closes under force and can pinch; x-cap.barisyazici.hand_stop.v1 is the safe_state=True action and @estop calls the native stop. Gate digest is the digest line the check printed; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run.
